messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that astronomers have confirmed in the entire observable universe is the exoplanet **HD 100546 b**. It orbits the young star HD 100546, located about 320 light‑years away in the constellation Musca.

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Radius** | ≈ 2.5 × Jupiter’s radius (≈ 170,000 km) |
| **Mass** | ≈ 10–20 × Jupiter’s mass (≈ 3–6 × 10²⁴ kg) |
| **Orbital distance** | ≈ 10 AU from its host star |
| **Age** | The system is very young (≈ 5–10 million years), so HD 100546 b is still forming and may be a “protoplanet.” |

Because it is still accreting material, its exact mass and radius are somewhat uncertain, but it remains the largest planet that has been directly imaged and whose properties have been measured. No larger planet has been found in the observable universe so far.
